title: Events API clients stop breaking when a page is deleted mid-scroll
whyNote: Three tickets in a fortnight, all the same shape: a row deleted between two pages of a cursor scroll drops the next page entirely.

acceptance.statement: A deleted row between two pages no longer drops the following page.
Existing `?page=` callers keep working and still get the deprecation header.
A cursor issued before this change still resolves for 30 days.

title: On-call handover writes itself from the shift's incidents
whyNote: Every handover is retyped from the incident list. Four minutes each, twice a day, and the detail people actually need gets left out when it is late.

acceptance.statement: The handover names every incident opened or still open during the shift.
An engineer can edit it before it is sent.
Nothing is sent without someone pressing send.

title: Release notes are drafted from the merged changes, not from memory
whyNote: The checklist has said `write the notes` for eleven releases. Six shipped without them.

acceptance.statement: Every merged change in the release appears in the draft.
The draft is editable before it is published.

title: A pull request that has waited two days says so, where reviewers look
whyNote: The oldest open PR was nine days. Nobody was ignoring it; nothing said it was old.

acceptance.statement: A PR older than the team's agreed window is visibly marked in the queue.

title: Incident severity is proposed from the symptoms, with the rule that chose it
whyNote: Severity is set by whoever opens the incident, and the handbook's table is three clicks away at the moment it matters.

title: A handbook page whose subject changed says it is out of date
A deploy inside the freeze window asks first
whyNote: CW-204 went out at 16:58 on a Friday. Nothing stopped it; nobody meant to.

title: Events API answers a cursor page in under 200ms at the 95th percentile

acceptance.statement: A cursor page answers in under 200ms at p95 on the production dataset.
No client had to change to get it.

title: An incident's timeline is built as it happens, not written up afterwards

acceptance.statement: Every status change and message lands on the timeline without anyone copying it.
The write-up is exportable at the end.
A private note stays out of the customer-facing export.

title: Does the review standard apply to generated code?
The on-call runbook links to the dashboards it names

acceptance.statement: Every dashboard named in the runbook is a link.

visuals.noVisualReason: Text-only change inside an existing page; the before and after differ by link markup.

title: A test that fails twice on unchanged code is quarantined, not retried forever
whyNote: Reruns cost about forty minutes of pipeline a day and teach everyone to ignore a red build.
